source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
NTT Ashburn VA1 Data Center in Ashburn, Virginia, publishes 12.6 MW of IT capacity, operated by NTT.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 1260 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 315 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for NTT Ashburn VA1 Data Center. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

Virginia has 26 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 20 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 1338.6 MW. NTT Ashburn VA1 Data Center contributes 12.6 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
